methodology_other:
Using a point tool, we asked 15 volunteers to categorise every one image on the Zooniverse platform. We asked volunteers to identify a road wadi crossing, and mark the length of the intersection with a line. 

We generated a consensus from the raw data, using a clustering algorithm called DBScan. The markings were validated by an expert by comparing the marks to satellite imagery within GIS.

To see more about the project, you can view it [here](https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/alicemead/sudan-road-access-logistics-cluster).
name: sudan-road-river-intersections
notes:
This is a line dataset of the locations where a wadi (dried river bed) intersects a key access road in Sudan. The line gives the length of which the road is impacted by the wadi. 

This information was produced to understand which roads maybe more affected during the rainy season, when wadis can fill with water quickly.

The dataset was produced in collaboration with the WFP Global Logistics Cluster. Please find more about the project [here](https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/alicemead/sudan-road-access-logistics-cluster).

organization.description: The Planetary Response Network has been running since 2014, working on providing rapid, accurate and high-value situational awareness to responders working in disaster relief. The project is partnered with Zooniverse, which is the online crowd sourcing platform used to host the projects. Zooniverse has over two million volunteers signed up to the website, with many other non-logged in volunteers taking part.
